blocks.html:
Hello — I’m aokuma.
Let me apologise up front for how long this page is. I would much rather over-explain than have you regret the purchase, and this is what that turned into.

This is the English edition of the introduction page. The full manual and the companion guides are still Japanese only for now.

blocks.text: 🌱 It started as a fork of “AI Slide Studio”

blocks.html:
The origin of this tool is “AI Slide Studio”, an excellent tool published by Majin. SlideCast Studio v1.0 was what came out after I took that prompt and modified it well past the point of reason.

It began as a weekend hack for my own use, and then I fell in. By the end it had reached a quality where even I — someone who would rather not stand out — thought it would be a waste to keep it to myself. So I worked up the nerve and sent Majin a DM.

Very generously, Majin published SlideCast Studio v1.0 as a guest post on their note, where it got a lot of response, and then went further and gave me permission to sell it on my own note. This tool exists in public because of Majin. Thank you, again.

blocks.html: Honestly, when v1.0 went out I was pleased with myself — “a solid 90 out of 100,” I thought. Then I kept using it, kept hitting things it couldn’t quite do, kept finding bugs I had missed, and quietly revised my own score: “more like a 30 or 40, in hindsight.” Closing those gaps produced v2.0, and steady work since then has brought it to v3.4 “NUANCE”.

sections.title: ❶ What SlideCast Studio can do
sections.intro: A slide-video tool that runs start to finish in the browser. Nothing to install.

blocks.html:
SlideCast Studio is a slide-video tool that runs entirely in the browser, with nothing to install.
Load PDFs, images or video, add AI voice (TTS), and it produces a video with narration and subtitles already in place.

You can save the result as video (MP4 / WebM), and also export it as presentation files (PowerPoint and friends) or as images.
Explainer videos for YouTube, vertical video for TikTok and Shorts, internal decks — all of it comes together startlingly fast.

sections.title: ❷ How you actually build one (no API key needed)
sections.intro: Prepare the material in Bundle Builder, finish it in SlideCast Studio. That is the short path.

blocks.title: 🌟 Start with Bundle Builder
blocks.text: SlideCast Studio Bundle Builder is a companion tool that runs inside Google Gemini Canvas. On the standard models it takes you from script writing all the way to AI voice generation without you obtaining an API key. Open it from the Bundle Builder card on the dashboard.

items.title: Prepare everything in Bundle Builder
items.text: Either have the AI generate the slide images on the spot, or upload PDFs and images you already have. From there: script generation → AI voice generation → validation, ending in a ZIP export. No API key registration involved.

items.title: Load the ZIP into SlideCast Studio
items.text: Drop the ZIP onto “Create from documents” on the dashboard. Slides, script and audio all come in together.

items.title: Shape the design and the performance
items.text: With the preview open, adjust subtitles, background, character, BGM, captions and transitions.

items.title: Export
items.text: One click on either [Export video] or [Export documents], depending on what you need. MP4 and WebM, plus PPTX, PDF, PNG and JPEG.

blocks.alt: The Bundle Builder script generation screen, with panels for audience, script style, number of speakers and subtitle line count
blocks.caption: Script generation in Bundle Builder. Pick the audience and the number of speakers, and you have a script

blocks.text: 🧩 What Bundle Builder handles for you

items: Generating the slide images themselves with AI (you specify topic, audience, slide count and art style)
Automatic script generation (up to six speakers, with control over subtitle layout and furigana)
Assigning a voice per speaker and generating all the audio in one pass
Replacing lines with microphone recordings (with head and tail trimming)
Automatic validation of script, speakers, audio and slide references
Exporting slides, script and audio together as a ZIP
Switching the UI between Japanese and English

blocks.title: 🟢 Too many settings? Try Simple mode
blocks.text: One switch reduces the screen to the minimum set of settings and fills in sensible defaults for the rest. Turn it off once you find your feet, and you are back in the full mode where everything is adjustable.

sections.title: ❹ System requirements
sections.intro: Please read this before buying, and go ahead only if it works for your setup.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Phones and tablets are not supported
blocks.text: This is a web app for desktop browsers, with Google Chrome recommended. Running it on a phone or tablet is neither intended nor supported.

items.label: Recommended browser
items.value: Google Chrome (desktop, current version) is the strongest recommendation; Microsoft Edge (current version) also works

items.label: Recommended OS
items.value: Windows 11 or later, or macOS 13 or later

items.label: Memory
items.value: 16 GB or more recommended (32 GB for long or high-resolution projects)

blocks.text: 📄 Roughly how many slides

blocks.html: There is no fixed slide limit in the tool. Rendering, however, runs on your own machine and uses your browser’s memory. How heavy a project feels depends not just on slide count but on output resolution, total running time and the weight of your assets.

blocks.title: 💡 About those numbers
items: They are rough guidance only, and will shift with asset size and video length.
If you are unsure about your machine, start with a 1080p export at standard quality.
Video export uses browser memory, so closing other work and spare tabs makes it more stable.

blocks.text: 📱 About video for TikTok, X and Instagram

blocks.html:
Because it exports at 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1, the tool works well for producing footage for TikTok, X and Instagram.

That said, an MP4 export is not automatically in the ideal state for every platform. Two files can both be MP4 and still use different compression inside — H.264 and H.265 being the common pair. Video export here depends partly on what the browser supports, so depending on your browser the MP4 may come out as H.265. When that happens, converting to H.264 is often the more reliable route for some platforms.

blocks.title: 📮 An assumption about posting to social platforms
blocks.text: Please use the tool on the assumption that a final pass — adjustment or format conversion — may be needed before you post.

sections.title: ❺ Where your data lives, and security
sections.intro: Projects are stored inside your own browser. Nothing is sent to an external server.

blocks.html: All project data is stored inside your own browser, in IndexedDB. Nothing is uploaded to an external server.

blocks.title: ⚠️ When data disappears
items: When you clear the browser’s history and cookies
When you uninstall the browser
When you close an incognito or private window
Once data is gone, the app cannot recover it. Regular backups are the only defence.

blocks.html: You can export and restore backups from the dashboard (v3.x added ZIP-format backups and a choice of what to include). If you open the app from a new Apps Script project or a different browser, your earlier data will not appear automatically — restore it from a backup.

blocks.text: 🔐 If you do use an API key

items: Never enter one on a shared PC or at an internet café
The API key is not stored in project data; it is kept only in the browser
Turn on “Do not store on this device (session only)” and it is discarded when you close the tab or browser
Setting usage limits and alerts in the Google Cloud Console is strongly recommended
A leaked and abused API key can result in a very large bill

sections.title: ❻ What it costs (buy once; API is optional)
sections.intro: The tool itself is a one-time purchase. An API key is an optional extra for people who want one.

before.label: 🛒 What you definitely pay
before.text: The one-time price of SlideCast Studio itself. There is no monthly charge and no subscription.

after.label: 🔑 What you might pay
after.text: If you want to generate AI voice with a single button inside the app, usage-based charges may apply on an API key you obtained yourself. This is optional.

blocks.text: 💡 How to run it with no extra cost at all

blocks.html: If you would rather not pay API fees, or the registration sounds like a hassle — that is fine. Every one of the following routes produces a narrated video without registering an API key.

items.title: Use Bundle Builder
items.text: Takes you all the way to AI voice with no API key configured. The recommended entry point (see ❷).

items.title: Use Google AI Studio directly
items.text: Have a Flash-tier TTS model with a free allowance (Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS or 2.5 Flash TTS) read the text, then import the saved audio files.

items.title: Bring voice from another service
items.text: Import audio files made with any other free or paid service.

items.title: Use your own voice
items.text: Import narration you recorded yourself. In-app microphone recording is also available (except in the GAS edition).

blocks.text: 🎙️ Rough costs when using your own API key

blocks.html:
To generate everything from inside the app with one button, register a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio in the settings screen. The free tier works for trying it out, but its per-minute and per-day request limits are tight, and generating dozens of slides at once can stall. For serious use, the paid tier fits better.

Gemini API TTS is not billed per request or per character. It is billed on input and output tokens, and the bulk of it is the generated audio side — roughly 32 tokens per second of audio.

blocks.title: 💡 How to choose a model
items: 3.1 Flash TTS Preview and 2.5 Pro Preview TTS are the same price on the official rate card ($1 input / $20 output per 1M tokens).
But 3.1 Flash has a free tier and 2.5 Pro does not. At equal prices, the newer model with a free allowance is the easy pick.
If cost is the only concern, 2.5 Flash Preview TTS at half the unit price is the cheapest.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Notes on these figures
items: The estimates assume 32 tokens per second of audio output, based on the official rate card as of August 2026.
Token costs on the text input side are not included.
Google’s pricing and specifications can change without notice. Always check the official rate card for current, accurate figures, and use the service at your own discretion.

blocks.label: Check the official Gemini API pricing

blocks.html:
If you would rather have a voice that is even and stable, even at the cost of expressiveness, you can optionally configure Google Cloud Text-to-Speech instead. It has a monthly free character allowance, and usage-based pricing beyond it.

Both are external services provided by Google. Please check Google’s own current terms and pricing.

sections.title: ❾ About the price (set by an AI, and variable)
sections.intro: I handed pricing over to an AI, and it will keep moving on the AI’s judgement.

blocks.html: Building this took about as much as I had to give. For the last several months my days have looked like this.

Nobody asked me to do this; I just wanted the tool to exist that badly. But between a day job and two small children, continuing to develop it at no return is not realistic. Charging for it is what lets it keep improving, and I hope you will read the decision in that light.

At the same time — I made it, so I want as many people as possible to actually use it. I know nothing about marketing, so I handed the pricing entirely to an AI, with the instruction to find a price that values the tool fairly, reaches as many people as possible, and still earns something.

So the price gets revised whenever the AI decides it should, based on how sales go and what has been added. If nothing sells it may come down; if it sells well or gains features it may go up. I genuinely do not know either.

blocks.text: Where the price stands now

blocks.html:
What the AI (Gemini 3.1 Pro) said:

  • Objective value of the tool: ¥10,000–15,000
  • Balancing reach against revenue: ¥3,980 as the floor

But putting myself in your position: “However useful it looks, handing about ¥4,000 to an individual developer I have never heard of takes some nerve.” And I really did want to put this in more people’s hands.

So I overruled the AI and set up a discount through note’s social-promotion feature. Share (repost) the article on X in support, and you can buy it for ¥1,980 — less than half the AI’s number.
(And if you are the sort of saint who buys at the regular ¥3,980 to support development, you are extremely welcome.)

blocks.text: This is the lowest an individual developer can go. I overruled the AI’s ¥3,980 and made it ¥1,980 with a share. In exchange, please be forgiving about the small early bugs 🙇‍♂️
blocks.cite: Where the AI and I landed

blocks.html: This special price will also drift towards whatever the AI considers fair as features and activity change. If you have been curious, now is a good moment to pick it up and try SlideCast Studio.
